chunk_map.heading: You steer the answer by loading context
The loop is what you repeat

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm prevented: a reader landing on a chunk cold, unable to resolve a pronoun/demonstrative to anything named so far. Closest case: chunk 3 line 19 'A role colors answers the same way a fact does' — 'a fact' resolves to the capital-of-Italy/lake-of-Finland facts named in chunk 2 (prior chunk of same file), not a forward or dead reference. Chunk 2 line 11 'Take a guess before it runs' — 'it' resolves to the second (dinner) prompt named two sentences earlier in the same chunk. No never-named or stranded referents found; harm absent.

Harm prevented: a chunk pointing at another file by position ('the opening lecture said') rather than by name/claim. No cross-file references of any kind appear in the body — the file is self-contained demo + framing prose. Rule has nothing to apply to.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm prevented: 'the X you did/saw/caught' pointing at a beat a re-chunk/rewrite stranded. This is the M1 opener (before the exercise per maintainer block: 'M1 opener, after Connections, before the exercise'), so chunk 4's 'Fix one trivial bug from your own backlog' is a FORWARD preview of the coming exercise, not a backward reference to a prior beat. No backward references to check.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read (guess-before-reveal)
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm prevented: the reveal printed above the guess line, so a reader can't experience the demo live. Chunk 2 line 11 'Take a guess before it runs. What does Claude suggest now?' precedes the reveal at line 13 'Something Finnish: salmon, rye bread, meatballs.' Order is guess-then-reveal within the same chunk, matching the maintainer block's standing constraint ('Guess before reveal... Both windows get narrated before the live run'). Harm absent.

Harm prevented: a chunk that says nothing standalone (a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet). Chunk 0 is a title-only H1 (compendium explicitly names this pattern 'title slide', not an orphan). Chunks 1-4 each carry multiple sentences of self-carrying content. No wait-state slides found.

Harm prevented: a header the chunk's own content contradicts. Closest case: chunk 1 'Who this is for' (line 3) is matched by its content (line 5, addressing the reader who already 'found this training'); chunk 2 'Context is King' is matched by the two-window demo showing context conditioning the answer; chunk 4 'The loop is what you repeat' is matched almost verbatim by its own closing line 27. No contradictions found.

Harm prevented: tics that read as machine-cadence at slide density (banned Not-X-Not-Y-Z, anaphora triples, self-grading superlatives, number+retraction, abstraction-noun stacks, empty-leg verb triplets). Checked each sub-item across all chunks: only single-leg 'Not' constructions found (line 19 'Not because Claude knows medicine...', line 27 'Not by reading about it.') — neither is the banned two-Nots-plus-Z pattern. No anaphora triples, no self-grading superlatives (self-grading-superlative sub-item, blocking), no number-plus-retraction, no abstraction-noun stacks, no empty-leg verb triplets. Harm absent on all sub-items.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm prevented: repo/authorial vocabulary (surface-as-noun, firing, compendium, forcing function, beat, mood, Connections-as-proper-noun) landing on a projected slide where a room engineer wouldn't recognize it. Scanned all body text — none of the listed dialect terms appear. 'The move' (line 21) is plain English, not repo dialect. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles only
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm prevented: bolded whole-sentence leads burning the emphasis budget on a narrative/demo slide. Scanned body for '**' — none found; all emphasis in the file is single-asterisk italics on quoted prompts (e.g. line 9 *"What is the capital of Italy?"*). Matches the maintainer block's standing constraint 'Zero bold on the narrative and demo slides.' Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm prevented: a phase-less prose section present in long-read but absent from the rendered Slides deck (the 2026-07-09 prework/supplementary-drop incident). Verified this file's include site: `grep -rn the-wizard-move curriculum/trainings/` shows it is pulled in via a standalone include-link at getting-going.md:42, inside that module's '## Start here' phase section (same structural pattern as every other AE101 lecture include, which is the pattern the 2026-07-09 fix restored module-wide). `node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js --file curriculum/lectures/the-wizard-move.md` → 'OK — 1 files, Phase/Step numbering consistent' and `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file ...` → '4 slides' counted, confirming the renderer sees all 4 content chunks, not a subset. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm prevented: hand-numbered headers or a broken 'Phase K'/'Step K' in-file reference. This file has no '## Phase N:' or '## N.' step headers (headings are claim-style: 'Context is King', etc.), and no numbered-step prose references. `node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js --file curriculum/lectures/the-wizard-move.md` → 'OK — 1 files, Phase/Step numbering consistent'. Rule has nothing to apply to.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm prevented: a positional pointer ('below', 'above', 'at the top of this page') aiming at a wall once the renderer cuts at ##. Ran `node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file curriculum/lectures/the-wizard-move.md` → 'OK — 1 files, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut.' Mechanical, verified this session. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm prevented: a dead in-deck fragment link, or an in-body link located by page geometry. `grep -n '\[.*\](' curriculum/lectures/the-wizard-move.md` returned no matches — the body contains zero markdown links. Rule has nothing to apply to.

Harm prevented: a slide that overflows on words or bullets and gets read off-screen or scrolled past. Ran `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/lectures/the-wizard-move.md` → 'files: 1  slides: 4  limits: 210 words / 6 bullets, oversized: 0 — every slide is within limits.' Mechanical, verified this session.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch (lecture = claims, exercise = imperative/phase label)
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm prevented: a heading in the wrong grammatical register breaking the imperative/claim split that signals mood-switch to the reader. 'Context is King' (chunk 2), 'You steer the answer by loading context' (chunk 3), and 'The loop is what you repeat' (chunk 4) are all assertive claims, matching the lecture register. Closest-to-violating case: chunk 1's 'Who this is for' (line 3) reads as a topical label rather than an asserted claim — it stays inside the rule because it functions as address-to-reader framing rather than an exercise-style imperative/phase label, and the rule's harm (imperative headings smuggling exercise mood into a lecture, or vice versa) is not present; no exercise-register heading appears anywhere in the file.

notes: Non-slides observation, out of scope for this class: chunk 1's heading 'Who this is for' is a topic label rather than a claim-style lecture heading (see rule 15 evidence) — noted as a borderline case, not filed as a finding since no harm from a wrong mood-switch was present.
